messages:
sam_cs: Sedgewater alerted — seeing a p99 spike on embeddings since ~05:20 UTC. p95 up ~300ms, p99s jumping to 4–5s for ~8% of requests. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/dash/embeds?org=sedgewater :alarm_clock:
alex_support: Got the customer on the line. They switched to batching=20 earlier today. Repro curl and trace id below. No code changes on their side otherwise.
sam_cs: sample trace: trace=trc_0a9e3c, host=gpu-34, route=/v1/embeddings, client_batch=20. Repro curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"input": ["..."], "batch_size":20}'
infra-bot: deploybot: runtime-service v1.12.0 deployed to us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T05:12:04Z.
ying_eng: FYI I merged PR #4827 that tightened KV cache eviction windows at 05:09 UTC (tries to free prefix cache more aggressively for embeddings). Might correlate.
maria_sre: Can someone grab host metrics (nvml, cpu steal), tenant queue depth and per-tenant concurrent requests for that window? Also need tail traces (both slow and normal) for comparison.
alex_support: grabbing logs now — seeing KV cache miss rate spike for tenant=sedgewater starting 05:18, and their requests are being routed to slower model-quantized fallback intermittently. Also observed per-tenant queue depth hit the 50-concurrency cap around 05:22.
sam_cs: customer says timeouts/slowdowns coincide with a background bulk job they run every 30m that spikes request concurrency for a minute — might be the noisy neighbor trigger.
maria_sre: ok hypothesis: batch size 20 + background burst -> cache churn + throttles -> requests miss hot KV cache -> fallback kernels -> long tail. Quick mitigation plan: 1) put Sedgewater on a short reservation/priority lane, 2) temporarily raise concurrency cap for them to smooth spikes, 3) run a cache-warm for their common prefixes. Anyone able to do 1+2 now?
alex_support: Applied short reservation: resv-78321 (10 min priority slot) and bumped tenant concurrency cap from 50 -> 80 for Sedgewater. Ran warm cache command: POST /internal/cache/warm?tenant=sedgewater&route=embeds (script attached). :white_check_mark:
sam_cs: After warm and reservation, p99 dropped to ~900ms within 90s; p95 back near baseline. Customer confirms much better UX.
ying_eng: Good. For a durable fix I propose we revert the aggressive eviction from #4827 (it freed shared prefixes too eagerly), and add tenant-aware warming + soft-reservation for customers doing large batched jobs. I can open revert + alternative PR.
maria_sre: Also recommend adding a per-tenant circuit breaker that prefers rejecting excess concurrency vs falling back to slower kernels — that reduces noisy tail impact on others.
customer_admin: thanks team — appreciate the fast patch. Any ETA on full fix? We run the bulk job every hour and want this prevented.
alyx_support: (typo note) meant alex_support above.
alex_support: ETA for hotfix + canary (revert + tenant-aware warm): 2–4 hours assuming no regressions. Will coordinate a small canary on 2 hosts then roll.
sam_cs: Next steps: 1) document incident in tracker + include traces (trc_0a9e3c, trc_0a9f12), 2) ying to open revert PR + soft-warm PR, 3) infra to monitor for regress, 4) recommend customer schedule their bulk job to a window or request a reserved slot if sustained.
maria_sre: I'll add temporary alerting for eviction-rate and per-tenant queue depth so we catch it earlier.
customer_admin: ok will try to push their job to a quieter window; thanks again.
sam_cs: Closing thread for now — reopen if we see recurrence. :handshake:
